D 7, 185 (1987); Voss, Weiss, Winkler, Physica B+C 123, 121 (1983)): not accessible. Bouazza et al. Z. Phys. D 7, 33 was read only through its first two pages (Springer preview, Tables 1 and 2).

conflicts: 5s 4P lifetimes: laser 4.5(5) ns (4P1/2) and 4.3(5) ns (4P3/2) (Bengtsson et al. 1992) vs beam-foil 3.6(4) and 3.8(4) ns (Andersen et al. 1974); laser values kept

Resonance-line f values: Bengtsson et al. 1992 print f(193.7 nm) = 0.123(17) and f(197.2 nm) = 0.059(8); the abstract of Berzins et al. 2021 prints '197.3 nm, f = 0.127, and 193.8 nm f = 0.059', i.e. the same two numbers attached to the opposite lines. Full text of Berzins et al. not accessible, so this was not resolved; Bengtsson's assignment agrees with NIST ASD (A = 2.19e8 and 2.02e8 s^-1)
NIST Handbook of Basic Atomic Spectroscopic Data (older) lists A = 2.2e8 (193.76 nm), 2.0e8 (197.26 nm) and 2.7e8 s^-1 (189.04 nm), from Morton 2000; consistent with the values here

Metastable lifetimes (theory only): MRCI 21(3), 248(4), 1.08(2), 0.47(1) s (Liu et al. 2023) vs 12-13, 143-177, 0.77-0.85, 0.34-0.55 s (Garstang 1964; Biemont and Hansen 1986); the forbidden-line A values entered under transitions are Garstang's and therefore correspond to the shorter lifetimes

Resolved (second pass, full text of Berzins et al. 2021 read): their Table 4 and abstract print f = 0.127(15) for 197.262 nm and f = 0.059(7) for 193.759 nm, but their own Table 3 A values (2.09e8 and 2.19e8 s^-1) give, derived here with f = 1.4992e-16 lambda^2[A] A g_u/g_l, f = 0.061 for 197.26 nm (J = 1/2 upper level) and f = 0.123 for 193.76 nm. The two f values are therefore attached to the wrong lines in Berzins et al.; the assignment of Bengtsson et al. 1992 kept in this file is the correct one.

Branching fraction of the 197.26 nm resonance line: 0.94(1) (Berzins et al. 2021) vs 0.907 (Lotrian et al. 1980, as quoted there); 4P1/2 - 2P°1/2 (307.5 nm) 0.0016(2) vs 0.0342. Berzins et al. A values vs NIST ASD: 245.65 nm 1.00e7 vs 7.2e6 s^-1, 249.29 nm 1.27e7 vs 1.2e7 s^-1.

Hyperfine A of 4p3 2P°1/2: 63.7(5) mK = 1909(14) MHz (Bouazza et al. 1987, kept) vs 75.0(6) mK = 2248(18) MHz (Voss et al. 1983, as quoted in Table 1 of Bouazza et al.). Other 4p3 levels agree (2P°3/2: 12(2) vs 12.9(6) mK; 2D°3/2: 16.0(3) vs 16(2) mK). The 4p3 constants already in this file (via Liu et al. 2023) were confirmed against Table 1 of Bouazza et al.
4p2 5s hyperfine A, Bouazza et al. 1987 vs Howard and Andrew 1985 (mK): 4P1/2 20.3(5) vs 23.0(8); 4P3/2 10.1(6) vs 8.8(5); 2D5/2 27.8(6) vs 28.9(5); others agree.

Lifetimes of 4p2 5s levels other than 4P1/2, 4P3/2: beam-foil 3.7(4) (4P5/2), 3.5(4) (2P1/2), 3.3(3) (2P3/2), 2.8(3) ns (2D5/2) vs theory 4.9, 2.6, 2.6, 3.1 ns (Holmgren, dipole length) vs values adopted by Berzins et al. 2021: 4.3, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0 ns. A values that the pipeline forms as branching / lifetime for these levels inherit this 20-30 % scale uncertainty (Berzins et al. Table 3 uses the adopted values and is therefore 14-17 % lower for 4P5/2 and 10-17 % higher for 2P).
notes: Level energies are the NIST ASD values (data/nist/As_I_levels.tsv). 75As has I = 3/2 and is the only stable isotope. The two resonance-line A values are derived from the absorption oscillator strengths printed by Bengtsson et al. (their laser lifetimes combined with the branching ratios of Lotrian et al. 1980); NIST ASD already lists the same numbers. Hyperfine A constants of the 4p3 2D, 2P levels are second-hand (Bouazza et al. 1987 as quoted by Liu et al. 2023); note the large uncertainty of 2P°3/2. Lifetimes of the 4p3 metastable levels and all forbidden-line rates are THEORY. In the forbidden-line entries A_s is the sum of the calculated M1 and E2 rates and the note gives both parts. Added 2026-10-01 (second pass): magnetic hyperfine constants A of the seven 4p2 5s levels (Bouazza et al. 1987, printed in mK and converted here, 1 mK = 29.979 MHz); 29 measured branching fractions of the 4p2 5s - 4p3 lines (Berzins et al. 2021, open-access copy on the University of Latvia server) and A values for the seven weak branches of the two laser-measured levels; second-hand beam-foil lifetimes for 4P5/2, 2P1/2, 2P3/2, 2D5/2 and a second-hand theory lifetime for 2D3/2. Berzins et al. print A as 'mantissa (power of ten)', e.g. '127 (5)' = 1.27e7 s^-1. Caveat on Bouazza Table 2: the row labels were read from a damaged OCR layer of the scan (rows in printed order: 4P1/2, 2P1/2, 4P3/2, 2P3/2, 2D3/2, 4P5/2, 2D5/2); the 4P3/2 and 2P3/2 labels are the least certain. Transitions between the quartet and doublet systems are typed 'intercombination'.
